Cost methodology \u2014 billed first, token model second\\n\\nBedrock bills **four token types**, each at its own unit price: input, output, cache read, cache write. Unit prices also differ by **service tier** (Standard, Flex, Priority \u2014 where published) and by **routing** (in-region vs `cross-region-global`). Summing only input and output tokens at one rate per model is the most common cause of totals that do not match the bill. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-understanding-cur-data.html, https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/\\n\\n**1a. Billed spend (Cost Explorer = billed truth).** Label these figures `(billed)`.\\n1. **Per model:** `aws ce get-cost-and-usage --group-by Type=PRODUCT_ATTRIBUTE,Key=model --metrics UnblendedCost UsageQuantity` (also `provider`, `inferenceType`, `feature`). Results come back keyed by display name (`model$Claude Sonnet 5`, `model$Nova Lite`); `model$` holds costs with no model. With `GroupBy`, each period\\'s `Total` is empty (`{}`): read the `Groups`, never take the empty `Total` as $0; a period with no `Groups` has no billed spend in that grouping. `Type=DIMENSION,Key=model` fails with `ValidationException`; product-attribute filters and `--dimension-key` are rejected by current CLI/SDK builds, so group rather than filter. Product-attribute data starts at a fixed date. A window that begins earlier fails with `DataUnavailableException`. Don\\'t assume the date: on that error, regroup the same window by `USAGE_TYPE` and say so. API: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-cost-management/latest/APIReference/API_GetCostAndUsage.html\\n2. **Per usage type** (any period): group by `USAGE_TYPE`. Lines encode model, token type, tier and routing, but naming varies \u2014 e.g. `USE1-NovaLite-input-tokens` vs `USE1-anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-mantle-input-tokens-standard` \u2014 so match a model\\'s lines loosely. `UsageQuantity` is often in thousands of tokens. Provisioned Throughput bills as model-unit hours, not tokens.\\n3. **Guardrail spend** bills as `USE1-Guardrail-*` usage types and appears in the `model$` product-attribute group. Label it as Guardrail cost and treat Guardrail posture as out of scope (see *Related skills (optional)* in `SKILL.md`).\\n4. **Service name:** do not filter on `SERVICE = \"Amazon Bedrock\"`. Bedrock costs can appear under more than one service name, so a single-name filter undercounts (`api-quirks.md` \u00a716). Omit the SERVICE filter with product attributes, or list names with `ce:GetDimensionValues` (`Dimension = SERVICE`, `SearchString = Bedrock`).\\n5. **Per caller / per application:** billed only with IAM principal attribution (CUR 2.0), application inference profiles, or project tags, each with cost allocation tags activated (allow up to 24 h to populate). Only the management (payer) account of an organization, or a standalone account, can view and activate cost allocation tags (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/custom-tags.html): `AccessDenied` on `ce:ListCostAllocationTags` from a member account is expected, not a permission to add; say the management account activates the tag key. Token model (cross-check and fallback).** Label these figures `(estimated)`.\\n1. Pull `InputTokenCount`, `OutputTokenCount`, `CacheReadInputTokenCount`, `CacheWriteInputTokenCount` (Sum) from `AWS/Bedrock`, by `ModelId`, over the window.\\n2. Multiply each token type by its rate. Read tier and routing from each row\\'s `usagetype` (contains `global` in any case = global; `flex`, `priority`; none = Standard) and skip rows containing `batch`, `custom-model`, `Customization`, `ProvisionedThroughput` or `reserved`. In testing, 5 calls priced all 5 models in use, Claude Sonnet 5 at $2.20/$11 per 1M (Standard), matching the bill. Match the exact model name and version as published (e.g. `Claude Sonnet 4.6`; `Claude Sonnet 5` \u2260 `Claude Sonnet 5.5`) and the region. Take the on-demand rate for the assumed tier (Standard, Flex, Priority) and routing (in-region, geographic, global); billed usage types show which apply (`-flex`, `-priority`, `-cross-region-global` / `_global_standard`; none of these = Standard). AWS documents that both are **0 when prompt caching is not used**, and that `InputTokenCount` excludes cached tokens. Cache writes are priced above normal input and reads below it, so caching saves money only when each written prefix is read back several times. Writes clearly above reads confirm this form: give both counts and the write:read ratio, and say the saving depends on the model\\'s write and read rates (price them per the token model, or say \"not priced\"). In testing, GPT-5.6 Terra wrote 4.4M and read 0.57M cache tokens in 14 days (7.7:1).
